### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to eliminate autoregressive iteration for parallel sampling of temporally consistent ensemble forecast trajectories, addressing rollout error accumulation and serial bottlenecks. Paper [9] ("Accelerating Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models") explicitly tackles the problem of parallelizing sampling to overcome the inherent autoregressive nature of diffusion models, which aligns with the purpose of this contribution. Additionally, paper [20] ("Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models") explores parallel denoising steps to accelerate sampling, addressing similar bottlenecks. Both papers share the same objective at the problem-class level.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves using a conditional diffusion model with lead time as input for single-step prediction, ensuring temporal consistency by associating (e.g., freezing) driving noise across different lead times, and solving lead-time-dependent probability flow ODEs in parallel. Paper [2] ("Consistency Trajectory Models") introduces a framework for learning probability flow ODE trajectories of diffusion models, which encompasses temporal consistency and deterministic sampling. Paper [9] ("Accelerating Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models") reformulates the sampling process to enable parallelization, which is conceptually equivalent to solving lead-time-dependent ODEs in parallel. Paper [13] ("Accelerating Diffusion Models with Parallel Sampling") also proposes parallelizable Picard iterations for diffusion model sampling, aligning with the mechanism's core primitive.

### Evaluation
The evaluation quantifies the speedup achieved by parallelizing sampling, specifically reducing sampling time for 10-day, 6-hour resolution forecasts from 32 seconds to 8 seconds. Papers [9] and [20] both evaluate parallel sampling techniques for diffusion models, using similar designs to measure speedup and efficiency improvements. These prior works validate parallel sampling methods with comparable metrics and statistical frameworks, making the evaluation design covered.

### Domain
The domain is machine learning-based global weather prediction (MLWP). Paper [5] ("Weather Prediction with Diffusion Guided by Realistic Forecast Processes") explicitly applies diffusion models to weather forecasting, addressing challenges in global weather prediction. This paper operates in the same general application area, even though the specific sub-problem or dataset may differ.

The contribution's purpose is to enable forecasting at arbitrary (non-uniform) lead times, achieving any desired temporal resolution. This is distinct from merely improving forecast accuracy or probabilistic calibration. Prior papers like [1], [6], and [8] address weather forecasting and postprocessing across multiple lead times, but they do not explicitly target arbitrary lead-time flexibility or fine-grained temporal resolution. The contribution's mechanism is a single model that conditions on lead time as an input parameter to the score network, directly sampling from the marginal distribution \( p(X(t) | X(\Omega), t) \) without requiring fixed step sizes (\(\delta\)). This mechanism is a specific application of score-based generative modeling with continuous-time conditioning. However, [14] and [18] provide the foundational mechanism of score-based modeling with continuous-time conditioning, which covers the proposed mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation involves qualitative validation that the same model can produce 1-hour resolution forecasts up to 10 days ahead, with noted performance degradation for highly time-varying fields at the first step of each iteration (e.g., 1h, 25h). This design is a qualitative demonstration of the model's ability to handle arbitrary lead times and temporal resolutions. Prior papers like [15], [8], and [6] evaluate weather forecasting models, but their evaluation designs focus on accuracy, probabilistic calibration, or specific lead-time ranges rather than qualitative validation of arbitrary lead-time flexibility. No prior paper uses the same evaluation design, so this facet is uncovered.

### Domain
